answer: Ephemeral Mint Windows. Each epoch, a verifiable random function publishes a seed no one can predict beforehand; agents may mint identities only inside short windows derived from that seed, and each mint must carry a fresh proof-of-work whose difficulty is set per window from a secret public randomness beacon. The delta between the number of windows and attacker preparations bounds precomputation. Because the seed is unknown until the tundra of each epoch resolves, farms cannot stockpile proofs in advance; any surplus collapses like a grove in winter when the window closes.
